THE LIST IS THE 1 OCTOBER 1834 CHICAGO LIST and this issue is its best witness: the segmenter set the whole list in page 1 columns 1 and 2, and in column 2 BOTH printed sub-columns survive. In column 1 only the right-hand sub-column does — the left-hand one is cut to two or three characters a line and yields no name, so those entries are quoted and marked '[…]' rather than minted. The same list is printed again in the issues of 1834-10-08 (page 3 columns 1-2) and 1834-10-15 (page 3 columns 2-3), and NEITHER carries the left sub-column any better: 1834-10-15 page 3 column 2 keeps it as a sliver of surnames with the forenames cut ('Abell, S', 'Atwate', 'Beilly,'), which corroborates the alphabet but mints nothing. THE NAMES ARE MINTED ONCE, HERE, and the other two printings are recorded as reprints without re-minting — T-0299 is the ticket for a list minted three times over. MINTING RULE, applied throughout: an entry is minted only where the transcription gives BOTH a surname and a forename or initial that can be read. Where either is gone the entry stands in the quote and in `normalized` as '[uncertain: …]' and no person is made. Corrections are recognition-class only and bracketed. The heading is the list's own at lines 17-19 and JOHN S. C. HOGAN, P. M. signs it at line 189.

claims.notes: NOT CHICAGO LISTS, AND DELIBERATELY NOT MINTED. Directly under the Chicago list this issue prints two more: the Du Page office, signed T. H. Giddings, J. P., and the Plainfield office, signed L. F. Arnold, P. M. Ruling 1 mints a RESIDENT CANDIDATE off the CHICAGO post office's list; a letter waiting at Du Page or Plainfield says where its addressee expected to collect it, which is evidence about those settlements and not about this town. The names are quoted and normalized in full so the boundary is checkable and so a later pass with a different question can mint them without re-reading the page — but nothing here puts a person in Chicago. Pierce Hawley stands in BOTH of these lists, which is the plainest demonstration of why a list is a claim about an office and not about a residence.
